jobs.title: Noir week, v
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 22, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Friday. The noir ends. The dog comes back. The trench coat goes in the wastebasket, on the page. Panel 1: a trench-coated figure at a table under a single lamp in a dark room, noir shadows, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD). caption box: "Friday. The case was going nowhere. Cases in Small Wood never went anywhere. That was the town's alibi.". Panel 2: a dark room, a door with a scratching sound drawn at its base, a man at a table looking up (in this panel: WOOD). caption box: "Then the door.". Panel 3: a small scruffy dog drawn in a light cartoon style standing in the doorway of a heavy noir room where a trench-coated figure sits staring at it, the two styles clashing in one panel (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: a young man's bedroom in ordinary cartoon style, a trench coat stuffed in the wastebasket, the young man at his table in a chore coat with a small dog on his foot, black and white (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Wood says, in a small balloon, "...It's called SLASH. It's going well.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
